title: Integral and rational bases from one compatible root tower
statement: Use the site and size convention [def-weil-size-convention], [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the root modules [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf], slice restriction [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] and the internal/sectionwise equivalence [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Fix a prime ell, a scheme X where ell is invertible in every residue field, a single object W of its small pro-etale site, and for every n >= 0 a section zeta_n of mu_(ell^(n+1))(W) and a module isomorphism e_n from the restricted constant Z/ell^(n+1) unit to the restricted root module. Assume the root power transition sends zeta_(n+1) to zeta_n, and that e_n sends every local scalar a on V -> W to a times the restriction of zeta_n. For each finite intermediate extension E of Q_ell in the fixed algebraic closure, the specific integral twist of [sk-def-sp-tate-twist] restricted to W is isomorphic to its coefficient unit, and the specific rational scalar extension restricted to W is isomorphic to its coefficient unit. Both isomorphisms are linear over their own restricted pulled-back condensed coefficient rings. In the internal/sectionwise encoding this says signed degree one is isomorphic to signed degree zero, separately for the integral and rational line. It asserts no covering family, finite-coefficient clause, or algebraic-closure twist clause.

proof.text: The section reconstruction equivalence preserves limits. Slice restriction preserves limits by evaluating on each object V->W: it is evaluation on the underlying V, which preserves sheaf-module limits. Apply the natural diagram isomorphism to the mapped twist limit cone. The normalized coefficient cone is also a limit, so uniqueness of limits identifies their vertices. Reconstructed regular internal coefficients identify with the section-module unit by the identity on sections. This yields the integral basis.

proof.text: Apply local basis preservation under scalar extension to the specified map O_E,X -> E_X and the integral twist. Degree one of spSignedTwist is its input line and degree zero its coefficient unit by their definitions. This gives exactly the rational basis as well as the integral conclusion.

theorem spIntegralRationalRootBasis
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime]
    [∀ x : X, Invertible (ℓ : X.residueField x)] (W : X.ProEt)
    (ζ : ∀ n : ℕ, (Scheme.purTwistRootsModule X ℓ n).val.obj (op W))
    (e : ∀ n : ℕ,
      (SheafOfModules.unit (Scheme.purTwistRing X (Scheme.purTwistFiniteRing X ℓ n))).over W ≅
        (Scheme.purTwistRootsModule X ℓ n).over W)
    (hζ : ∀ n : ℕ,
      (Scheme.proEtaleRootsOfUnityTransition X (ℓ ^ (n + 1)) (ℓ ^ (n + 2))
        (pow_pos (Fact.out : ℓ.Prime).pos _) (pow_pos (Fact.out : ℓ.Prime).pos _)
        (pow_dvd_pow ℓ (Nat.le_succ (n + 1)))).hom.app (op W) (ζ (n + 1)) = ζ n)
    (he : ∀ (n : ℕ) (V : (Over W)ᵒᵖ)
      (a : ((Scheme.purTwistRing X (Scheme.purTwistFiniteRing X ℓ n)).over W).obj.obj V),
      (e n).hom.val.app V a =
        a • (Scheme.purTwistRootsModule X ℓ n).val.map V.unop.hom.op (ζ n))
    (E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField ℓ) :
    Nonempty ((spSignedTwist X _ (spIntegralTwist X ℓ E) 1).over W ≅
      (spSignedTwist X _ (spIntegralTwist X ℓ E) 0).over W) ∧
    Nonempty ((spSignedTwist X _ (spRationalTwist X ℓ E) 1).over W ≅
      (spSignedTwist X _ (spRationalTwist X ℓ E) 0).over W)
